questions.q: What determines whether a user can see a page or function at all, like Manage Invoices?
options: The security profile alone
The job role and its bundled function privileges
The accounting period status
The data role's scope
questions.explain: Job roles and their function privileges control whether a page or function is visible/usable at all, separate from which data it can act on.

questions.q: What determines which specific business units, ledgers, or legal entities a user's access actually covers?
options: The data role and its attached security profile
The job role name alone
The browser being used
The invoice amount
questions.explain: Data roles combine a job role with a specific data security grant, and the security profile defines the actual scope (such as business units) that grant covers.

questions.q: Why did the fact that the clerk could open Manage Invoices (but saw zero results) point toward a data access issue rather than a function privilege issue?
options: It didn't — it still could have been either
Because Manage Invoices never requires any privilege
Because zero results always means a network error
Because the page loading and search working confirmed function privilege was fine; the problem had to be in which data the role was scoped to
questions.explain: Since the function itself worked, the investigation could focus specifically on the data role's security profile rather than re-checking function privileges.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the clerk not seeing Westfield Campus invoices?
options: The invoices were all on hold
The clerk's job role lacked AP privileges entirely
The clerk's data role had a security profile scoped only to Riverside Campus, because the account was provisioned from a template built for a different business unit
The business unit didn't exist yet
questions.explain: The clerk's account was set up from a Riverside Campus template and the business unit scope was never updated to include Westfield Campus, which the clerk actually needed.

questions.q: Why does the lesson caution against simply adding every business unit to the clerk's security profile to make the symptom disappear?
options: Because Oracle limits the number of business units per profile
Because access should be scoped to what the role actually needs, confirmed with the manager, rather than over-granting broad access
Because adding more business units is technically impossible
Because it would automatically disable the job role
questions.explain: The correct fix scopes access to the business unit(s) actually needed for the role, rather than over-provisioning access just to resolve the immediate complaint.
